name: spec
description:
Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.35.0 — design doctrine cut and source-gate feed retirement (specs/20260824/05-design-doctrine-cut.md), closing the five-spec render-gate series (specs/20260824/01–05, ADR-0002: fidelity is judged at the render, never by diffing source): `spec/doctrine/design.md` is rewritten to five sections (Design Canon, Design Authoring Contracts, Design Render Gate, Design Atlas, Workflows Encode Shape, Not Judgment), capped at 160 lines, contracts a script enforces or a worker applies only — the source-grep fidelity gate's history, the Fable retainer, the vision consult, skeleton binding maps, delta rows, and the exit fidelity review are gone from doctrine along with the mechanism itself. `spec/scripts/dc-extract.js` and `spec/scripts/fidelity-check.js` are deleted with their tests and their `spec-paths`/`entrypoints.json` entries. The `.design/` sidecar's remaining traces are retired: `init-gen.js` no longer emits its gitignore line, this repo's own `.gitignore` and `.claude/spec-manifest.json` claim drop it, `doctor.md` drops its orphan-sidecar check, and `spec.md`'s UI-section and `design_source` comments are rewritten to the render-gate flow. `grounding-contract.md`'s `design.copyCatalogs`/`design.screenshot` become legacy-tolerated, unread keys under a new § Render gate heading — the render gate judges painted text, never source copy. 
7.34.0 — design rules execute on the render (specs/20260824/04-render-rules.md): `design-rules.json` entries gain an optional `renderCheck` object (`target-size {min}`, `cta-count {max, tokens[]}`, `contrast {min, minLarge}`, `palette {}`) that the new `render-rules.js` (`spec-paths render-rules`) executes over render inventories — box vs threshold for target-size, token-resolved background count for cta-count, WCAG 2.x luminance ratio for contrast, `tokens.css`-resolved membership for palette — printing `rule <id> <kind> …` findings, a `source-side=<n>` count for rules without a `renderCheck`, and `unresolvable --name` lines for tokens.css values it can't parse (exit 0/1/2). `render-inventory.browser.js` gains `effectiveBackground` and `fontWeight` per entry (additive, `schemaVersion` unchanged) so contrast has a real background to check against. `render-gate.js` runs `render-rules.js` over every component inventory when the host config declares `design.rulesManifest`, and gains a `--mocks <mock>…` mode that captures mocks only (no ledger, no component URL, no comparison) and runs the rules over them. `/spec:sketch`'s exit now runs `render-gate --mocks` after the expansion pass and before the ratify question — a rule finding blocks ratification until the mock is fixed or the rule is amended, never excused per surface — replacing the Sonnet rule-checklist walk there, in `/spec:review`'s design legs (the advisory render-gate run now carries the rules), and in `design.md`'s harness paragraph. `spec/templates/design-rules.json` gains four `renderCheck` examples (`min-target-size`, `one-primary-cta`, `text-contrast-aa`, and `palette` on `no-raw-color`) for hosts to copy and hand-edit; `/spec:doctor` warns nothing about the field (out of scope, brief 11). The genesis-family rule-checklist walk survives only at the explore stage, which precedes `design-rules.json` and so has no manifest to execute (`genesis-explore.md`); `genesis.md` is corrected to say so and to drop its now-false claim that the walk also runs at review. Adopting `render-gate --mocks` for explore candidates stays waived to brief 10. 
7.33.2 — mock hygiene and the sketch-exit matrix (specs/20260824/03-mock-states-hygiene.md): `design-atlas.js check` gains four hygiene checks, bound at `data-status` `ratified` or `approved` (or under `--matrix`), free at `sketch`: a universal `box-sizing: border-box` rule in the mock's own `<style>`; every CSS block declaring `font-size` also declares `line-height`; the `[data-screen-label]` root's class rule(s) declare neither `border` nor `border-radius`; every `data-state-btn` control sits before the root's opening tag or inside a `data-contract="none"` ancestor — and a `<style>` with unbalanced braces is a violation naming the file, never a silent skip. `ratified` and `approved` are now equivalent for every check the atlas runs (matrix rules included); the atlas keeps both badge names — `ratified` is roadmap-level provenance, `approved` is standalone-spec-level provenance. `/spec:sketch`'s exit now runs the expansion pass (media queries + the tokens dark block) and `check --matrix`, rendering the matrix screenshots for a fast confirm, before the ratify question — so on roadmap-derived mocks the matrix is confirmed once, at ratification, rather than again at `/spec:design` promotion. The mock mark vocabulary (`data-screen-label`, `data-status`, `data-state-btn`, `data-contract="none"`, `data-positioned`) is now documented in `design.md`'s harness paragraph, and the roadmap-brief template's `surfaces` comment is corrected from the stale `regionRef` reference to `data-screen-label` anchors.
